title: Layout with flexbox
lesson:
To put boxes **side by side**, make their parent a **flex container**:

```
.row { display: flex; gap: 12px; }
```

Every child of `.row` now sits in a row with 12px between them. The useful extras:
- `flex-wrap: wrap;` lets items drop to the next line when there's no room (essential on phones).
- `justify-content` spaces items along the row: `space-between`, `center`, `flex-start`.
- `align-items` lines them up across: `center`, `flex-start`, `stretch`.
- On a child, `flex: 1` means "share the leftover space"; `flex: 1 1 200px` means "start at 200px, grow and shrink as needed", which gives a grid of cards that reflows by itself.
- `flex-direction: column` stacks instead of rows.

A header with a title on the left and buttons on the right is three lines: `header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }`.

(For two-dimensional grids there's also `display: grid`, which you'll meet in Level 2.)
